strings.title: Install GBS Reimagined
strings.lead: Install the firmware on a RetroScaler GBS-C from this page and connect the board to your Wi-Fi. You need Chrome or Edge on a computer and a USB data cable.
strings.none: This site has no firmware to install yet. To serve your own build, run uv run tools/release/installer_site.py --build, then build the site again.
strings.unsupported: This browser cannot use the computer's serial ports. Open this page in Chrome or Edge on a computer: phones and tablets cannot install.
strings.notAllowed: The installer only works over HTTPS or from this computer (localhost).
strings.step1: Plug the board's micro-USB port into the computer with a USB data cable.
strings.step2: Click Install, choose the board's port (named USB-SERIAL CH340 or similar) and click Connect.
strings.step3: Choose "Install GBS Reimagined". The first time, tick "Erase device", so that nothing from the previous firmware is left behind, then choose "Next" and "Install". A board that already runs GBS Reimagined is offered "Update GBS Reimagined" instead, which keeps its settings, profiles and Wi-Fi.
strings.step4: When "Installation complete!" appears, choose "Next". After an erase, the dialog asks for your Wi-Fi network: choose it, type its password and choose "Connect". Once the board has joined, "Visit Device" opens the board's page.
strings.step5: To set up Wi-Fi later, choose "Skip" on that form: the board opens its own network, named GBS- and four characters, password qqqqqqqq. Join it and open http://192.168.4.1.
strings.updateBody: A board on your Wi-Fi updates from its own page: System, Firmware update. This page can also update it over USB, keeping its settings.
strings.troubleNoPort: No port in the list: try another cable (some only charge) and another USB port. On Windows, the board's USB chip, a WCH CH340, may need the maker's driver.
strings.troubleBusy: "Failed to open serial port": close every other program that uses the port (Arduino IDE, PlatformIO, a serial monitor), then try again.
strings.troubleWifi: The board does not join the network: check the password, and that the network is 2.4 GHz (the board has no 5 GHz radio). To try again, click Install: the dialog finds the running board and offers "Connect to Wi-Fi" or "Change Wi-Fi".
strings.troubleStopped: The installation stopped halfway: click Install and start again. The chip's own loader, which the installer talks to, is never written, so an install over USB can always be repeated.
